events.text:
🇮🇷 Iran's new battle tactics threaten to shut down Hormuz traffic
Forces from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps are now targeting ships' engine rooms instead of other parts of the hull. The sustained damage typically brings a vessel to a halt and requires lengthy repairs, and in some cases has caused the ship[ to sink entirely](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76493). Iran has repeatedly warned that unauthorized passage through the Strait of Hormuz exposes ships to Iranian attacks.
To carry out these strikes, Iran has reportedly begun relying more heavily on anti-ship missiles and drones equipped with infrared guidance, according to a recent Bloomberg article. IR guidance allows the weapon to home in on the hot engine room on its own, without depending on radio signals that are easy to jam.
The shift matters because high gasoline prices remain a political vulnerability for Donald Trump, despite efforts to ramp up oil exports. The new attacks deter shipowners from attempting the crossing and undercut US claims that trade through the strait is returning to normal.

🇮🇷🇮🇱 Netanyahu’s top general resists attempts to restart war with Iran – report
Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has ostensibly refused to carry out an unspecified military action that could "trigger a rapid escalation into a confrontation with Iran," Israeli Channel 12 reported on October 25.
Zamir sought further deliberations and a written authorization for the op, with Israeli generals suspecting that their country’s leadership may be attempting to “utilize the Iranian issue for political benefit.”
Netanyahu himself vehemently denied the report and insisted that Zamir himself said that Iran allegedly sought to interfere in the Israeli election.
Earlier last week, Israeli Channel 13 reported that Zamir said that he does think it is necessary to attack Iran before the elections in Israel.
🔊 "We do not see any indications of a need to strike Iran before the elections. If we determine that a strike on Iran is necessary, we will strike," Zamir remarked.
This development takes place amid speculation that Netanyahu may be seeking to resume the war with Iran, either to boost his chances of reelection or to delay the election.
Some online sleuths even claim that recent flights from Israel to Cyprus may indicate an ongoing evacuation of high-ranking Israeli officials ahead of a new round of Israel-Iran fighting.
